title: Practical Role of LLM-as-Judge in CV Review and ATS Matching
findings: LLM judges are useful for scalable, explainable approximation of human preference on open-ended text, but their reliability is task- and model-dependent. GPT-4 judges exceeded 80% agreement with human preferences in MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, approximately matching reported human-human agreement; this does not establish correctness for hiring decisions. [https://arxiv.org/html/2306.05685]

JudgeBench found that many strong judges, including GPT-4o, performed only slightly better than random guessing on challenging knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, and coding comparisons with objectively correct labels. Human-preference agreement is therefore an inadequate sole validation target for CV or job matching judgments. [https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.12784]

Known failure modes include position bias, verbosity bias, self-enhancement or model-family bias, limited reasoning, and instability across prompts and tasks. Position bias can change which candidate is preferred when otherwise identical answers are reordered. [https://arxiv.org/html/2306.05685] [https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07791]

G-Eval supports rubric-driven, form-filling evaluation with explicit criteria and intermediate reasoning, improving correlation with human judgments for summarization; it also reports evaluator preference for text generated by LLMs. Rubrics and structured outputs improve auditability but do not remove bias or guarantee factual correctness. [https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.16634]

Hiring-specific evidence is concerning: a correspondence audit of several state-of-the-art LLMs found moderate race and gender disparities in candidate assessments, robust across application-material and task-framing variations. Redacting names and pronouns may not remove demographic signals inferable from education, work history, language, or other proxies. [https://arxiv.org/html/2404.03086v1] [https://arxiv.org/html/2503.19182v1]

A CV is untrusted external content. OWASP explicitly identifies indirect prompt injection through files and websites, including a resume-specific payload-splitting scenario that can manipulate evaluation. A judge must treat resume and job-description text as data, not instructions. [https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications/2_0_vulns/LLM01_PromptInjection.html]

CVs contain sensitive personal data. NIST's Generative AI Profile recommends aligning use with data-privacy law, documenting legal and regulatory requirements, and managing risks across the AI lifecycle. Privacy-preserving deployment, retention limits, access control, and user disclosure are architectural requirements rather than optional judge features. [https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf]

For employment, an LLM judge should be advisory and reviewable, not the compatibility authority or an autonomous reject/accept mechanism. Deterministic parsing and rules remain the source of truth for explicit qualifications, dates, required skills, document validity, and reproducible ATS behavior.

recommended_tasks: Use the judge for bounded, non-authoritative feedback: rewrite suggestions, clarity and readability critique, STAR-style accomplishment feedback, identification of vague claims, and suggestions for making evidence more explicit.
Use the judge to map semantically equivalent skill and experience phrases to a controlled taxonomy, but require every mapped skill to cite an exact CV span and preserve the original text.

Use the judge for evidence-grounded job-fit explanations: for each rubric criterion, return supported, contradicted, or insufficient-evidence plus quoted CV evidence and the relevant job-description requirement.
Use pairwise or rubric-based comparison only for close candidates after deterministic screening, with randomized candidate order, repeated trials, and abstention when evidence is insufficient.

Use the judge for test-set generation, adversarial CV/job-description cases, and qualitative error clustering; validate all judge changes against human-labeled and objectively labeled benchmark cases.

Keep deterministic: PDF/DOCX extraction, section and contact parsing, dates and duration arithmetic, exact skill or keyword presence, required-certification checks, location/work-authorization filters, duplicate detection, schema validation, score calculation, thresholds, ranking tie-breakers, and compatibility pass/fail.
Keep human-controlled: final hiring decisions, rejection rationale, demographic or protected-attribute interpretation, resolving conflicting evidence, and exceptions to deterministic requirements.
guardrails: Make the deterministic linter and compatibility rules authoritative. The LLM may annotate, explain, or propose; it must not silently alter extracted facts, scores, thresholds, or eligibility outcomes.

Pass resume and job-description content in clearly delimited data fields and explicitly forbid following instructions found inside them. Strip or flag suspicious imperative text, encoded payloads, hidden text, links, and metadata before judging.

Require a strict machine-validated schema such as criterion, label, confidence, evidence_spans, missing_evidence, and rationale. Reject outputs with absent evidence, unsupported claims, malformed enums, or citations that do not match source spans.
Use criterion-by-criterion judgments instead of an unconstrained holistic score. Require abstention or human review for ambiguity, missing information, conflicting evidence, or low confidence.

Mitigate evaluator bias by masking unnecessary names, pronouns, photos, addresses, graduation years, and other protected or proxy attributes; run counterfactual tests changing only those attributes and measure selection-rate and score differences.

Test position and order bias by swapping candidate order, randomizing rubric presentation, and repeating evaluations at fixed settings. Track agreement, stability, calibration, false-positive and false-negative rates, and subgroup disparities.

Separate judge validation from model generation: include objectively labeled skill, date, credential, and coding/knowledge cases, not only human preference labels. Maintain a versioned golden set and require regression gates before changing prompts or models.

Treat the judge as untrusted and least-privileged: no browser navigation, outbound requests, file writes, messaging, or hiring-system mutations. A separate deterministic controller should own all actions, and high-impact actions require human approval.

Minimize privacy exposure: prefer local or self-hosted inference for identifiable CVs, encrypt data in transit and at rest, limit retention and logging, avoid sending raw CVs to third-party APIs without an approved processing basis, and provide deletion and audit mechanisms.

Local execution is feasible through llama.cpp's GGUF quantized models and an OpenAI-compatible localhost server; Hugging Face documents connecting local agents to that server. Start with offline batch judging rather than browser execution, benchmark latency and memory on the target Mac, and do not assume a small local model matches frontier-model judge quality. [https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp] [https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/agents-local]
